q.hi: 8 engineers ki team naya product bana rahi hai, domain abhi clear nahi. Site ke hisaab se kya architecture?
q.en: A team of 8 engineers is building a new product and the domain is not clear yet. Which architecture per the site?

hi: Shuru se 20 microservices with service mesh
Microservices par sabka ek shared DB
Modular monolith; boundaries pakki hon aur load alag ho tab services nikaalo
Har feature ke liye alag serverless function
en: 20 microservices with a service mesh from day one
Microservices sharing one database
A modular monolith; extract services once boundaries are clear and load differs
A separate serverless function per feature

why.hi: Chhoti team me ops ka bojh features se zyada ho jaata hai, aur galat boundary = distributed monolith.
why.en: For a small team the ops burden outweighs features, and a wrong boundary gives a distributed monolith.

q.hi: Mobile app ko kam fields aur ek call chahiye, web ko zyada data. Kya lagaoge?
q.en: The mobile app needs fewer fields in one call; the web needs more data. What do you add?

hi: BFF (Backend for Frontend): har client type ka alag chhota backend
API Gateway me client-specific business logic
Service mesh sidecar
Client-side service discovery
en: BFF (Backend for Frontend): a small backend per client type
Client-specific business logic in the API Gateway
A service mesh sidecar
Client-side service discovery

why.hi: Gateway sirf cross-cutting kaam (auth, rate limit, routing) kare; client-specific shaping BFF me, ideally frontend team ke paas.
why.en: The gateway does only cross-cutting work (auth, rate limiting, routing); client-specific shaping goes in a BFF, ideally owned by the frontend team.

q.hi: Order → Payment → Inventory → Notification sab sync REST call chain hai, har ek 99% available. End-to-end availability aur sahi fix?
q.en: Order → Payment → Inventory → Notification is a sync REST chain, each 99% available. End-to-end availability and the right fix?

hi: 99%, kyunki sab parallel chalte hain
~96%; har service ko ek shared DB do
99.99%; retries sab theek kar denge
~96% (0.99⁴); notification jaise kaam async events pe, baaki pe timeout + circuit breaker
en: 99%, because they all run in parallel
~96%; give every service one shared DB
99.99%; retries fix everything
~96% (0.99⁴); move work like notification to async events, add timeouts + circuit breakers on the rest

why.hi: Lambi sync chain me availability multiply hoti hai aur latency add. "Ho gaya" batane wala kaam async rakho.
why.en: In a long sync chain availability multiplies and latency adds up. Keep "it happened" work async.

q.hi: Purane monolith se payments nikaalna hai bina big-bang rewrite. Strangler fig ke steps ka sahi order?
q.en: You must pull payments out of an old monolith without a big-bang rewrite. Correct order of strangler fig steps?

hi: Monolith band karo → naya service deploy → DB migrate
Proxy aage lagao → payment service banao → traffic shift (shadow → canary → 100%) → monolith ka code hatao
Naya service banao → clients ko seedha naye URL pe bhejo → proxy baad me
Monolith ka DB naye service ke saath share karo, phir kabhi alag mat karo
en: Shut the monolith → deploy the new service → migrate the DB
Put a proxy in front → build the payment service → shift traffic (shadow → canary → 100%) → delete the monolith code
Build the new service → point clients straight at its URL → add a proxy later
Share the monolith DB with the new service and never split it

why.hi: Routing layer se feature-by-feature migration, migration ke dauraan CDC sync. Shared DB coupling wapas le aata hai.
why.en: A routing layer enables feature-by-feature migration with CDC sync during the move. A shared DB brings coupling back.

q.hi: CQRS aur Event Sourcing ka relation kya hai?
q.en: What is the relationship between CQRS and Event Sourcing?

hi: Ek hi cheez ke do naam
Alag cheezein hain; CQRS normal DB + outbox/CDC se bhi chal sakta hai
Event Sourcing ke bina CQRS possible nahi
CQRS sirf Kafka ke saath kaam karta hai
en: Two names for the same thing
They are different; CQRS can run on a normal DB + outbox/CDC
CQRS is impossible without Event Sourcing
CQRS only works with Kafka

why.hi: CQRS = alag read/write models. Event sourcing = state ki jagah events store. CQRS akela common hai; ES sirf jahan history hi product ho.
why.en: CQRS = separate read/write models. Event sourcing = store events instead of state. CQRS alone is common; ES only where history is the product.

q.hi: User ne order place kiya par Elasticsearch wali order list me turant nahi dikha. Site ka recommended handling?
q.en: A user placed an order but it does not show up in the Elasticsearch order list immediately. Recommended handling?

hi: Read model ko har write pe synchronously update karo, distributed transaction se
CQRS hata do
Client ko 5 sec sleep karke reload karne do
Write response me naya data lautao aur critical read ("order hua?") write DB se karo
en: Update the read model synchronously on every write with a distributed transaction
Remove CQRS
Have the client sleep 5 seconds and reload
Return the new data in the write response and serve the critical read ("did my order go through?") from the write DB

why.hi: Read model eventual hai (ms–seconds peeche). UI write response se dikhao, version field se staleness batao.
why.en: The read model is eventual (ms to seconds behind). Show the UI from the write response and expose staleness via a version field.

q.hi: Wallet event-sourced hai. Do requests ek saath same balance pe ₹120 spend karti hain. Double spend kaise rokoge?
q.en: A wallet is event-sourced. Two requests spend ₹120 against the same balance at once. How do you stop a double spend?

hi: Append pe `expected_version` check (unique `(stream_id, version)`); ek fail hoga aur retry karega
Har 100 events pe snapshot lo
Upcaster lagao
Read model se balance padh ke validate karo
en: Check `expected_version` on append (unique `(stream_id, version)`); one fails and retries
Take a snapshot every 100 events
Add an upcaster
Validate against the balance from the read model

why.hi: Optimistic concurrency: dono ne version N padha, sirf ek N+1 likh payega. Read model eventual hai, us pe validate karna unsafe.
why.en: Optimistic concurrency: both read version N, only one can write N+1. The read model is eventual, so validating against it is unsafe.

q.hi: `MoneyAdded` event me naya field add karna hai. Lakhon purane v1 events hain. Sahi tareeka?
q.en: You need a new field on the `MoneyAdded` event. There are millions of old v1 events. Right approach?

hi: Migration script se saare purane events rewrite karo
Purane events delete karke snapshot se shuru karo
`MoneyAdded v2` banao; purane v1 events padhte waqt upcaster unhe v2 shape me convert kare
Field ko read model me hi add karo, events ko chhodo
en: Rewrite all old events with a migration script
Delete old events and start from a snapshot
Create `MoneyAdded v2`; an upcaster converts old v1 events to the v2 shape when reading
Add the field only to the read model and ignore events

why.hi: Events immutable hain; rewrite audit trail todta hai. (GDPR ke liye crypto-shredding: per-user key phenk do.)
why.en: Events are immutable; rewriting breaks the audit trail. (For GDPR use crypto-shredding: throw away the per-user key.)

q.hi: 2 node failures sehne hain. Raft cluster me kitne nodes chahiye?
q.en: You must survive 2 node failures. How many nodes does a Raft cluster need?

hi: 5 (2f + 1, majority 3)
en: 5 (2f + 1, majority 3)

why.hi: f failures ke liye 2f + 1. 4 ya 6 nodes extra failure tolerance nahi dete, bas writes slow karte hain.
why.en: 2f + 1 for f failures. 4 or 6 nodes add no extra fault tolerance, just slower writes.

q.hi: Raft me followers ka election timeout randomized (jaise 150–300 ms) kyun hota hai?
q.en: Why is the follower election timeout randomised (e.g. 150–300 ms) in Raft?

hi: Taaki clock skew theek ho
Taaki leader ke heartbeats compress ho sakein
Taaki sab ek saath candidate na banein aur split vote kam ho
Taaki committed entries kabhi overwrite na ho
en: To correct clock skew
So leader heartbeats can be compressed
So nodes do not all become candidates at once and split votes are rare
So committed entries are never overwritten

why.hi: Ek node pehle timeout hoke votes le leta hai. Split vote hua to candidate dobara timeout pe naya term try karta hai.
why.en: One node times out first and collects votes. On a split vote the candidate retries in a new term after another timeout.

q.hi: Raft me client write kab "committed" maana jaata hai?
q.en: When is a client write considered "committed" in Raft?

hi: Jab leader apne log me likh de
Jab entry majority ke log me aa jaaye
Jab saare followers ack kar dein
Jab next heartbeat chala jaaye
en: When the leader writes it to its own log
When the entry is in the log of a majority
When every follower acks
When the next heartbeat is sent

why.hi: Majority (3 me 2) ka ack kaafi hai; slow follower baad me catch up karta hai. Naya leader wahi banta hai jiske paas sab committed entries hain.
why.en: A majority ack (2 of 3) is enough; a slow follower catches up later. Only a node with all committed entries can become the new leader.

q.hi: Scheduler leader etcd lease se chuna jaata hai. Purana leader 20 sec GC pause se jaaga, lease expire ho chuki thi, aur woh write karta hai. Ise kya rokta hai?
q.en: A scheduler leader is chosen with an etcd lease. The old leader wakes from a 20 s GC pause after its lease expired and writes. What stops it?

hi: Fencing token: har naye lease ke saath badhta number; storage purane token wali write reject kare
Lease TTL badha do
Gossip protocol se membership track karo
Heartbeat interval kam kar do
en: A fencing token: a number that grows with each new lease; storage rejects writes with an older token
Increase the lease TTL
Track membership with a gossip protocol
Reduce the heartbeat interval

why.hi: Quorum minority ko leader banne se rokta hai, par "late write" ke liye fencing token chahiye (Raft term, ZK zxid). Token 33 aa chuka to 32 reject.
why.en: Quorum stops a minority from becoming leader, but a "late write" needs a fencing token (Raft term, ZK zxid). Once 33 is seen, 32 is rejected.
